subject: SIG Questionnaire: subprocessor exceptions & cryptographic evidence package
body:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@hightowerhealth.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: security@hightowerhealth.com
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG questionnaire follow-up — subprocessor exceptions and crypto proofs

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for taking our SIG request. We got the preliminary answers, but the auditors asked for a consolidated index of evidence that ties each SIG control to an artefact (policy, log slice, attestation). They also flagged a few subprocessor items listed as "exception" — specifically any vendor that does not have dedicated key separation or uses shared KMS across tenants.

Can you provide: 1) a single spreadsheet that maps SIG control IDs -> evidence filename/link; 2) a CSV of subprocessor exceptions with a brief mitigation/compensating control for each; and 3) any proof of key separation or crypto custody for the affected processors (redacted as needed).

We're on a tight audit window (closing 10/25). If you can outline what you can deliver by EOD 10/20 that would be great.

Appreciate it —
Alex Turner
Head of InfoSec — HighTower Health

---
On Sun, Oct 18, 2026 at 11:03 AM Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com> wrote:
From: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@hightowerhealth.com>
Cc: security@hightowerhealth.com, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 11:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire follow-up — subprocessor exceptions and crypto proofs

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the clear ask. We can do that. High-level plan:

- Deliverable A: "sig3_evidence_index_v1.xlsx" — single-sheet mapping of SIG3 control IDs to evidence filenames and short notes on scope.
- Deliverable B: "redwood_subprocessor_exceptions.csv" — list of processors flagged as exceptions, reason for exception, mitigation and planned remediation ETA.
- Deliverable C: zip of redacted cryptographic custody proofs (we will include a short, signed statement per vendor and a KMS ownership snapshot).

I'll coordinate S3 access log slices and the KMS snapshot with Ben and Karthik. We expect a first-pass index and exception CSV by 10/20 EOD PT, final proofs as soon as legal signs off on redactions.

Naomi Feldman
Senior Security Liaison, Redwood Inference
---
On Mon, Oct 19, 2026 at 10:15 AM ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com> wrote:
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 10:15:03 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire follow-up — subprocessor exceptions and crypto proofs

Naomi / Karthik — quick ops note: I pulled a bounded slice of S3 access logs for the "inference-model-artifacts" bucket covering Aug–Sep (attached stub: s3_access_logs_slice-202609.csv). Also exported the KMS key metadata for tenant-key aliases (kms_key_holdings_proof.txt).

For the exception CSV: there are three processors that require exceptions right now: (1) model-shipping-cdn (uses a partner KMS for edge replication), (2) thirdparty-annotations (contractually multi-tenant, no per-customer key), (3) analytics-pipeline (legacy HSM integration pending migration).

I've added short mitigation notes in the draft CSV and flagged planned remediation quarters. I can run a redaction pass on KMS metadata (remove ARNs) once legal confirms format.

Ben
Director, Customer Security Operations
Attachment(s): s3_access_logs_slice-202609.csv (stub), kms_key_holdings_proof.txt (stub)
---
On Mon, Oct 19, 2026 at 14:42 Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 14:42:27 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire follow-up — subprocessor exceptions and crypto proofs

Ben / Naomi — thanks for the heads-up. A couple of clarifications for the index:

- Can we include a column "evidence_confidence" with values (policy, artifact, live_log, attestation)? Auditors find that helpful.
- For the model-shipping-cdn exception, we should attach the partner's attestation summary (we have one on file from 2025-11) and cite the routing policy that prevents customer PI from being cached.
- I'll prepare a short signed statement (internal) that describes the crypto custody model for Redwood-managed keys vs partner-managed keys; that will go into the proofs bundle.

I'll take the lead on building the sig3_evidence_index_v1.xlsx if Ben can push the CSV/logs into the shared Drive folder. Naomi — can you confirm the Drive link and whether Legal needs to review the redaction format?

Karthik
Senior Applied Security Engineer
---
On Tue, Oct 20, 2026 at 17:45 Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com> wrote:
From: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@hightowerhealth.com>
Cc: security@hightowerhealth.com, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: SIG questionnaire follow-up — deliverables (initial bundle)

Alex —

Attached is the initial evidence bundle for your SIG review. Summary of what we delivered:

1) sig3_evidence_index_v1.xlsx (attached) — single-sheet mapping of SIG3 control IDs to evidence items. Column legend included; evidence_confidence uses values: policy, artifact, live_log, attestation.
2) redwood_subprocessor_exceptions.csv — three current exceptions (model-shipping-cdn, thirdparty-annotations, analytics-pipeline) with mitigation notes and remediation windows.
3) kms_key_holdings_proof.txt — redacted snapshot of KMS metadata plus a signed internal statement describing separation of duties and key custody practices.
4) s3_access_logs_slice-202609.csv — limited log slice to substantiate access controls for the model artifacts bucket.

A couple of caveats: the KMS metadata file is intentionally redacted for ARNs and account IDs; if your audit needs full ARNs we can arrange a secure, in-person log review or add a notarized attestation from our partner (subject to NDAs).

If the auditors want more granular telemetry (per-request KMS logs matched to user IDs) please let me know and we'll assess feasibility; that typically requires extended retention settings and we can queue a job but it will take extra time.

Next steps: confirm receipt and whether the auditor needs full ARNs or the redacted bundle is sufficient. We'll be on standby for any follow-ups.

Best —
Naomi Feldman
Senior Security Liaison, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment(s): sig3_evidence_index_v1.xlsx (stub), redwood_subprocessor_exceptions.csv (stub), kms_key_holdings_proof.txt (stub), s3_access_logs_slice-202609.csv (stub)
